why: Identity and RELATEDNESS are different questions. A shared Alt ID whose relation is IsDerivedFrom says the identifier names a DIFFERENT work, so it is not evidence the two records are the same and must never carry a cross-type pair to Accept. But it IS evidence they are ABOUT each other, so when other metadata already agrees the pair is lifted into Review for a human rather than discarded. This is the theatrical-short-vs-registry-Episode shape: seven NE4 rows regressed to a terminal no-match when eidr-core 0.22.0 made matches identity-only, and human review had confirmed every one as a match. The floor can only raise a score INTO the Review band, never to Accept -- that asymmetry is why a relatedness signal is safe here and would not be safe in the corroboration path. Guard ordering is what this pins: the cross-type gate must cap first and the floor must lift second.
